ei.title: A Journey From War to the Olympics
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
When Yusra Mardini was a young girl growing up in Damascus, Syria, her life centered around swimming. Her father was a former professional swimmer, and she started learning how to swim from a young age. When she was nine years old, she was already faster than many older swimmers. It was clear that she had a special talent, and she fell in love with the sport. She enjoyed watching Olympic swimming events with her father, which led her to dream about competing in the Olympics. She got the chance to represent Syria in an international swimming championship, and it seemed like her Olympic dream might someday come true.

However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be a wake-up call for Yusra and her sister Sara. They realized that they could no longer stay in their home country, and they made up their minds to flee Syria and go to Germany to avoid the war. If they reached Europe, the rest of the family would follow. The decision was not an easy one, but Yusra knew that it was her only option if she wanted to pursue her dream and live without fear.

In August, 2015, the sisters began their dangerous journey by making their way to their first destination, Türkiye. There, along with 18 other people, including children and babies, they boarded a tiny boat designed for seven passengers. They were heading across the sea towards Greece when disaster struck. The boat's engine failed in the middle of the open sea, and the weather rapidly grew worse. The heavy boat began to sink, and the panicked, desperate passengers had no choice but to throw their possessions into the sea. Yusra felt heartbroken as she watched people's treasured belongings disappear under the waves. However, she had no time to reflect. She had to take action immediately in order to save herself and the other passengers. She jumped into the water along with Sara and two others, and the four of them guided the drifting boat. They swam for three and a half hours until they arrived safely with all the other passengers on the shore of a Greek island.

Next, Yusra and Sara had to travel through Macedonia, Serbia, Hungary, and Austria. They walked great distances, and even though they caught rides in small cars and crowded buses from time to time, they had to cross every border on foot. No matter how exhausted they were, they kept moving. At the end of this overwhelming 25-day journey, they finally made it to Germany and settled at a refugee center in Berlin. Despite all the hardships and adversities she underwent, Yusra's passion for swimming never left her. In fact, it was the only thing she could do to feel at home in this foreign land.

She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center and asked if he could be her coach. When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her outstanding talent and agreed to do so. Sven helped Yusra stay focused and persistent in her efforts to pursue excellence. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would pay off one day.

Yusra soon received a chance to make her dream a reality when she was invited to join the first ever refugee team at the 2016 Summer Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro. Although it seemed like a great opportunity, Yusra was hesitant. If she joined the refugee team, she thought, people might view her with pity instead of seeing her as a serious athlete. She almost turned down the invitation, but she decided to accept it after she realized that she could inspire hope in millions of other refugees facing similar challenges.

At the Games, Yusra competed in both the 100-meter butterfly and the 100-meter freestyle events. When she stepped onto the starting blocks, she was determined to pour everything she had into the competition. She came in 41st out of 45 competitors in the butterfly and 45th out of 46 in the freestyle event. Even though she left the Olympics without a medal, she was proud to have made history alongside her teammates. The time on the scoreboard did not matter. In one interview, when a reporter asked if she could make a statement, she remarked, "I want everyone to stay strong for their goals in life, because if you have your goals in front of your eyes, you will do everything you can; and I think even if I fail, I will try again. ... I want to show everybody that it's hard to arrive at your dreams, but it's not impossible. You can do it; everyone can do it."

questions.passage: When Yusra Mardini was a young girl growing up in Damascus, Syria, her life centered around swimming. Her father was a former (A)[professional / amateur] swimmer, and she started learning how to swim from a young age. When she was nine years old, she was already faster than many older swimmers. It was clear that she had a special (B)[talent / weakness], and she fell in love with the sport. She enjoyed watching Olympic swimming events with her father, which led her to dream about (C)[competing / surrendering] in the Olympics.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 전직 프로(professional) 수영 선수였고, 특별한 재능(talent)이 있었으며, 올림픽에서 경쟁하는(competing) 꿈을 꿨다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① professional — talent — competing: 원문 일치
❌ ② amateur: professional의 반의어
❌ ③ weakness: talent의 반의어
❌ ④ surrendering: competing의 반의어
det.tip: professional(전문적인) ↔ amateur(아마추어). talent(재능) ↔ weakness(약점). competing(경쟁) ↔ surrendering(포기).

questions.passage: In August, 2015, the sisters began their (A)[dangerous / safe] journey by making their way to their first destination, Türkiye. There, along with 18 other people, including children and babies, they boarded a tiny boat designed for seven passengers. The boat's engine failed in the middle of the open sea, and the weather rapidly grew worse. The heavy boat began to sink, and the (B)[panicked / calm] passengers had no choice but to throw their (C)[possessions / hopes] into the sea.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ dangerous — panicked — possessions: 원문 일치
❌ ① safe: dangerous의 반의어. 위험한 여정임
❌ ② calm: panicked의 반의어. 배가 가라앉아 공황 상태
❌ ④ hopes: possessions가 원문. 소지품을 바다에 버린 것
det.tip: dangerous(위험한) ↔ safe(안전한). panicked(공황의) ↔ calm(침착한). possessions = belongings(소유물).

questions.passage: No matter how exhausted they were, they kept moving. At the end of this overwhelming 25-day journey, they finally made it to Germany and settled at a refugee center in Berlin. Despite all the hardships and adversities she underwent, Yusra's (A)[passion / indifference] for swimming never left her. In fact, it was the only thing she could do to feel at home in this foreign land. She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full (B)[potential / limit]. Sven helped Yusra stay focused and (C)[persistent / careless] in her efforts to pursue excellence. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would pay off one day.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 수영에 대한 열정(passion), 최대 잠재력(potential)에 도달, 끈기 있는(persistent) 노력.
det.analysis:
✅ ② passion — potential — persistent: 원문 일치
❌ ① limit: potential이 원문. 한계가 아니라 잠재력
❌ ③ indifference: passion의 반의어. 수영을 떠나지 않았으므로 열정
❌ ④ careless: persistent의 반의어. 끈기 있게 노력함
det.tip: passion(열정) ↔ indifference(무관심). potential(잠재력) ↔ limit(한계). persistent(끈기 있는) ↔ careless(부주의한).

questions.passage: Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became ①<u>risky</u>. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became ②<u>dangerous</u>. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was ③<u>horrifying</u> enough to be a wake-up call for Yusra and her sister Sara. They made up their minds to ④<u>remain</u> Syria and go to Germany to avoid the war.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① risky(위험한): 원문 일치. 학교 가는 것이 위험
✅ ② dangerous(위험한): 원문 일치. 수영도 위험
✅ ③ horrifying(소름 끼치는): 원문 일치. 폭탄 사건
❌ ④ remain(남다) → flee(도망치다): 전쟁을 피해 시리아를 '떠나기로' 결심한 문맥
det.tip: flee(도망치다) ↔ remain(남다). 'made up their minds to flee Syria'가 원문.

questions.passage: Yusra soon received a chance to make her dream a reality when she was invited to join the first ever refugee team at the 2016 Summer Olympic Games. Although it seemed like a great opportunity, Yusra was ①<u>hesitant</u>. If she joined the refugee team, she thought, people might view her with ②<u>admiration</u> instead of seeing her as a serious athlete. She almost turned down the invitation, but she decided to ③<u>accept</u> it after she realized that she could ④<u>inspire</u> hope in millions of other refugees facing similar challenges.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① hesitant(망설이는): 원문 일치. 난민팀 합류를 망설임
❌ ② admiration(존경) → pity(연민): 진지한 선수가 아니라 '동정'의 시선으로 볼까 걱정 ← 정답
✅ ③ accept(수락하다): 원문 일치. 초대를 수락
✅ ④ inspire(고무하다): 원문 일치. 다른 난민들에게 희망을 불어넣다
det.tip: pity(연민, 동정) ↔ admiration(존경, 감탄). 'instead of seeing her as a serious athlete'이 단서.

questions.passage: She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center. When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her ①<u>outstanding</u> talent and agreed to do so. Sven helped Yusra stay ②<u>focused</u> and persistent in her efforts to pursue ③<u>excellence</u>. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would ④<u>pay</u> one day.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'pay off(성과를 거두다)'인데, 'pay'만 사용하여 'off'가 빠졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① outstanding(뛰어난): 원문 일치. 뛰어난 재능
✅ ② focused(집중하는): 원문 일치. 집중력 유지
✅ ③ excellence(탁월함): 원문 일치. 탁월함을 추구
❌ ④ pay(지불하다) → pay off(성과를 거두다): 노력이 '결실을 맺기를' 바랐다
det.tip: pay off(성과를 거두다, 결실을 맺다) ≠ pay(지불하다). 숙어 구별 주의.

questions.passage: However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be a wake-up call for Yusra and her sister Sara. They realized that they could no longer stay in their home country, and they made up their minds to ____ Syria and go to Germany to avoid the war.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② flee(도망치다): 전쟁을 피해 시리아를 떠나기로 결심
❌ ① defend(방어하다): 떠나는 것이지 방어가 아님
❌ ③ rebuild(재건하다): 문맥상 떠나는 상황
❌ ④ celebrate(축하하다): 전쟁 상황과 맞지 않음
det.tip: flee = escape = run away from (도망치다). 전쟁을 피해 떠나는 문맥.

questions.passage: Next, Yusra and Sara had to travel through Macedonia, Serbia, Hungary, and Austria. They walked great distances, and even though they caught rides in small cars and crowded buses from time to time, they had to cross every border on foot. No matter how exhausted they were, they kept moving. At the end of this overwhelming 25-day journey, they finally made it to Germany and settled at a refugee center in Berlin. Despite all the hardships and ____ she underwent, Yusra's passion for swimming never left her.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ adversities(역경): hardships와 병렬. 원문 일치
❌ ① privileges(특권): hardships와 병렬이 안 됨
❌ ② comforts(안락함): 25일간 힘든 여정과 모순
❌ ④ victories(승리): hardships와 병렬이 안 됨
det.tip: adversity(역경) = hardship(고난). 원문: hardships and adversities.

questions.passage: At the Games, Yusra competed in both the 100-meter butterfly and the 100-meter freestyle events. When she stepped onto the starting blocks, she was ____ to pour everything she had into the competition. She came in 41st out of 45 competitors in the butterfly and 45th out of 46 in the freestyle event. Even though she left the Olympics without a medal, she was proud to have made history alongside her teammates. The time on the scoreboard did not matter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① determined(결심한): 경기에 전력을 다하겠다는 의지
❌ ② reluctant(꺼리는): 전력을 다하려는 문맥과 모순
❌ ③ confused(혼란스러운): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ indifferent(무관심한): 모든 것을 쏟아붓는 것과 모순
det.tip: determined = resolved = firmly decided (결심한). 'pour everything'과 호응.

questions.passage: However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the <u>horrors</u> of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 horrors와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ terrors(공포): horrors와 동의어
❌ ① blessings(축복): horrors의 반의어
❌ ② pleasures(기쁨): horrors의 반의어
❌ ③ advantages(이점): horrors와 무관
det.tip: horror = terror = dread (공포, 참상). 전쟁의 참상을 뜻함.

questions.passage: She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center and asked if he could be her coach. When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her <u>outstanding</u> talent and agreed to do so.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 outstanding과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ exceptional(뛰어난): outstanding과 동의어
❌ ① ordinary(평범한): outstanding의 반의어
❌ ② mediocre(평범한): outstanding의 반의어
❌ ④ average(보통의): outstanding의 반의어
det.tip: outstanding = exceptional = remarkable (뛰어난). 반의어: ordinary, mediocre, average.

questions.passage: The heavy boat began to sink, and the panicked, <u>desperate</u> passengers had no choice but to throw their possessions into the sea. Yusra felt heartbroken as she watched people's treasured belongings disappear under the waves.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 desperate와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② hopeless(절망적인): desperate와 동의어
❌ ① hopeful(희망적인): desperate의 반의어
❌ ③ relaxed(여유로운): desperate의 반의어
❌ ④ patient(인내심 있는): 절박한 상황과 모순
det.tip: desperate = hopeless = in despair (절망적인). 배가 침몰하는 극한 상황.

questions.passage: Although it seemed like a great opportunity, Yusra was <u>hesitant</u>. If she joined the refugee team, she thought, people might view her with pity instead of seeing her as a serious athlete. She almost turned down the invitation, but she decided to accept it.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 hesitant와 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① decisive(단호한): hesitant의 반의어
❌ ② uncertain(불확실한): hesitant의 동의어
❌ ③ cautious(조심스러운): hesitant의 유의어
❌ ④ doubtful(의심스러운): hesitant의 유의어
det.tip: hesitant(망설이는) ↔ decisive(단호한). uncertain, cautious는 hesitant과 비슷한 뜻.

questions.passage: No matter how exhausted they were, they kept moving. At the end of this <u>overwhelming</u> 25-day journey, they finally made it to Germany and settled at a refugee center in Berlin.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 overwhelming과 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ manageable(감당할 수 있는): overwhelming의 반의어
❌ ① exhausting(지치게 하는): overwhelming의 유의어
❌ ② intense(극심한): overwhelming의 유의어
❌ ③ staggering(놀라운): overwhelming의 유의어
det.tip: overwhelming(압도적인, 감당 안 되는) ↔ manageable(감당할 수 있는). exhausting, intense는 비슷한 뜻.

questions.passage:
(A) She enjoyed watching Olympic swimming events with her father, which <u>led</u> her to dream about competing in the Olympics.

(B) When Yusra Mardini was a young girl growing up in Damascus, Syria, her <u>life</u> centered around swimming.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 두 단어 led와 life의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 올림픽 꿈을 꾸게 했다(led). (B) 삶(life)이 수영 중심이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) ~하게 하다 — (B) 삶: led her to dream = 꿈꾸게 했다, life centered around = 삶이 ~중심
❌ ① (A) 이끌다: 물리적 인도가 아님. lead + 목적어 + to부정사 = ~하게 하다
❌ ② (A) 이끌다: 같은 이유
❌ ④ (B) 목숨: her life centered around swimming은 '삶'이지 '목숨'이 아님
det.tip: lead: ① 이끌다(물리적) ② ~하게 하다(원인). life: ① 삶 ② 목숨 ③ 생명.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어를 고르시오.

"a person who is forced to leave their country in order to escape war, persecution, or natural disaster"

det.korean: "전쟁, 박해, 또는 자연재해를 피해 자국을 떠나야 하는 사람" → 난민(refugee)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ refugee(난민): 정의와 정확히 일치
❌ ① athlete(운동선수): 스포츠 관련
❌ ② volunteer(자원봉사자): 자발적 참여자
❌ ④ competitor(경쟁자): 대회 참가자
det.tip: refugee(난민): refuge(피난처) + -ee(~하는 사람). 이 글의 핵심 주제.

questions.passage: Sven helped Yusra stay focused and __________ (persist) in her efforts to pursue excellence.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: ✅ persistent: persist(동사) → persistent(형용사). focused and _____ 병렬 구조에서 형용사 필요.
det.tip: persist → persistent: -ent 접미사. focused(형용사)와 병렬이므로 형용사 필요.

questions.passage: Even though she left the Olympics without a medal, she was proud to have made history alongside her teammates. The time on the scoreboard did not matter. In one interview, when a reporter asked if she could make a __________ (state), she remarked that she wanted everyone to stay strong.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: ✅ statement: state(동사) → statement(명사). make a _____ 구조에서 명사 필요.
det.tip: state → statement: -ment 접미사. make a statement = 성명을 발표하다.

questions.passage: Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be a wake-up call for Yusra and her sister Sara. They realized that they could no longer stay in their home country, and they made up their minds to flee Syria. The decision was not an easy one, but Yusra knew that it was her only option if she wanted to ____ her dream and live without fear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① pursue(추구하다): 꿈을 포기하지 않고 독일로 떠난 이유 ← 정답
❌ ② abandon(포기하다): 꿈에 매달리는 문맥과 모순
❌ ③ forget(잊다): 꿈을 잊는 것이 아님
❌ ④ ignore(무시하다): 꿈을 무시하지 않음
det.tip: pursue = chase = go after (추구하다). 'clung to her dream'이 단서.

questions.passage: Yusra felt heartbroken as she watched people's treasured belongings disappear under the waves. However, she had no time to ____. She had to take action immediately in order to save herself and the other passengers. She jumped into the water along with Sara and two others, and the four of them guided the drifting boat.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② reflect(숙고하다): 원문 일치. 즉시 행동해야 했기에 생각할 시간 없음
❌ ① celebrate(축하하다): 위기 상황에서 축하와 무관
❌ ③ relax(쉬다): 문맥과 무관하지 않으나 원문은 reflect
❌ ④ surrender(항복하다): 즉시 행동한 것이지 항복이 아님
det.tip: reflect = think deeply = contemplate (숙고하다). 'had no time to reflect'가 원문.
